nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used ordinary least squares regression to model the effects of age, gender, site, and optionally global thickness on regional cortical thickness in healthy controls. ROI thicknesses were regressed on these covariates to derive predicted values, and z-scores were calculated by subtracting predicted values from observed values and dividing by the standard error of regression.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: ROI thicknesses were regressed on age, gender, and site (only study 2 included site) in HCs to model the effects of normal aging, gender, and site. ... Regional thickness values were transformed to adjusted z scores by subtracting predicted values from observed values and dividing by the HC model standard error of regression.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Hua2025.pdf.md: METHODS AND MATERIALS / z-Scoring Normalization

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study modeled regional cortical thickness measures derived from 34 Desikan-Killiany atlas regions. Global mean cortical thickness was also computed. FreeSurfer was used to compute both global mean cortical thickness and ROI thicknesses.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Global mean cortical thickness and ROI thicknesses were computed using FreeSurfer (ROIs are numbered in figures and listed with assigned numbers in Table S2).
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Hua2025.pdf.md: METHODS AND MATERIALS / MRI Processing
